# title: ENG-205 Beowulf Part 3 — 5 Q&A
# topic: Beowulf Part 3 (to the end)
# short: 5 Q&A
# order: 5
# expect: 39
What does the Danish coast-guard receive as the Geats leave?
column2: The coast-guard receives a sword with gold fittings.

column1: Who is Hygelac's queen?
column2: Hygelac's queen is Hygd, the daughter of Haereth.

column1: Which cruel queen is contrasted with Hygd?
column2: Hygd is contrasted with Modthryth, who had men killed for looking at her.

column1: Who changed Modthryth's ways?
column2: Her husband, King Offa, changed Modthryth's ways.

column1: Who is Freawaru?
column2: Freawaru is Hrothgar's daughter, promised in marriage to Ingeld.

column1: Why does Beowulf doubt that Freawaru's marriage will bring peace?
column2: Beowulf expects an old Heathobard warrior to see a looted sword and stir up revenge.

column1: Which Geat did Grendel kill first?
column2: Grendel first killed and ate Handscio.

column1: What did Grendel carry to hold his victims?
column2: Grendel carried a pouch made of dragon skins.

column1: What does Beowulf give Queen Hygd?
column2: Beowulf gives Hygd the torque from Wealhtheow and saddled horses.

column1: What does Hygelac give Beowulf?
column2: Hygelac gives Beowulf Hrethel's sword, land, a hall, and a throne.

column1: How did the Geats view Beowulf when he was young?
column2: The Geats thought he was a weakling who lacked force.

column1: How does Hygelac die?
column2: Hygelac is killed on a raid into Friesland.

column1: Why does Beowulf not take the throne right after Hygelac's death?
column2: Beowulf chooses to support Hygelac's young son Heardred instead.

column1: Who kills Heardred?
column2: The Swedish king Onela kills Heardred.

column1: What wakes the dragon?
column2: A runaway slave steals a gold cup from its hoard.

column1: Why does Beowulf think the dragon's attacks are his fault?
column2: Beowulf fears he has broken God's law.

column1: What kind of shield does Beowulf take to fight the dragon?
column2: Beowulf takes a shield made entirely of iron.

column1: Who guides Beowulf to the dragon's barrow?
column2: The thief who stole the cup guides them against his will.

column1: Why does Beowulf tell his men to stay back?
column2: Beowulf says the fight is his alone and he will win the gold or die.

column1: Who is the only warrior to help Beowulf against the dragon?
column2: Wiglaf is the only warrior who helps Beowulf.

column1: What makes Wiglaf decide to help Beowulf?
column2: Wiglaf remembers the gifts Beowulf gave him and the loyalty he pledged.

column1: What happens to Naegling?
column2: Naegling snaps when Beowulf strikes the dragon's skull.

column1: Where does the dragon wound Beowulf?
column2: The dragon sinks its fangs into Beowulf's neck.

column1: Who strikes the dragon's belly?
column2: Wiglaf stabs the dragon low in the belly.

column1: What weapon does Beowulf use to finish the dragon?
column2: Beowulf kills the dragon with a knife from his belt.

column1: What does the dying Beowulf ask Wiglaf to bring him?
column2: Beowulf asks Wiglaf to bring out the treasure so he can see it.

column1: Where does Beowulf ask to be buried?
column2: Beowulf asks for a barrow on the headland at Hronesness.

column1: What does Beowulf give Wiglaf before he dies?
column2: Beowulf gives Wiglaf his gold collar, helmet, and mail shirt.

column1: What does Wiglaf say will happen to the deserters?
column2: Wiglaf says they will lose their lands and live in disgrace.

column1: What does the messenger predict after Beowulf's death?
column2: The messenger predicts that the Franks and the Swedes will attack the Geats.

column1: What happens to the dragon's treasure in the end?
column2: The treasure is buried with Beowulf in his barrow.

column1: Who sings a lament at Beowulf's pyre?
column2: A Geat woman sings a lament foretelling her people's ruin.

column1: Who killed Herebeald?
column2: His brother Haethcyn killed Herebeald by accident with an arrow.

column1: Why could Hrethel not avenge Herebeald?
column2: The killer was Hrethel's own son, so the law of the blood-feud could not be applied.

column1: How do the Geats describe Beowulf at the very end?
column2: They call him the kindest of kings to his people and the keenest to win fame.

column1: Who says "A warrior will sooner die than live a life of shame"?
column2: Wiglaf says it while condemning the warriors who deserted Beowulf.

column1: What passage in Part 3 is an example of ubi sunt?
column2: The last survivor's lament over his vanished people is an ubi sunt passage.

column1: How is the comitatus broken at the end of the poem?
column2: Beowulf dies without an heir, and his thanes are left leaderless and open to attack.

column1: What are Beowulf's enemies in old age, according to the course?
column2: In old age his enemies are his own pride and thanes who look out for themselves.
